title: L1G Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Covered Persons
tiers.description: All directors (executive and non-executive), officers, employees and contractors of the Company, First Maven Pty Ltd, L1 Capital, Platinum, members of the Platinum Compliance Committee, 50%+ owned Entities, GLS and LSF, plus all directors of any L1 Group company. All substantive prohibitions (Closed Trading Periods, short-term trading, hedging and short selling) apply without differentiation.

tiers.name: Platinum Covered Persons
tiers.description: Platinum Investment Management Limited's employees and contractors; distinguished only for pre-clearance and trade confirmation, which they obtain under Platinum's own Business Rules of Conduct rather than this policy's process.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, non-executive directors of LSF or GLS, and external members of the Platinum Compliance Committee; distinguished only for pre-clearance and trade confirmation, made via c&l@platinum.com.au.

tiers.name: All other Covered Persons
tiers.description: Employees and contractors of L1 Capital Pty Ltd who are not otherwise Directors; distinguished only for pre-clearance (L1 Capital Head of Legal and Compliance via the L1 Assured system) and trade confirmation (uploaded to L1 Assured).

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or the Company's Due Diligence Committee may determine any other 'black-out period'; confidentiality is not addressed.

rules.detail: L1G Securities expressly includes 'financial products (e.g. derivatives) that are issued or created by third parties' over L1G shares, so trading a third-party (OTC) derivative is a Trade requiring pre-authorisation (route depends on employer entity), outside Closed Trading Periods and the short-term window, and only while not aware of inside information. A derivative that operates to hedge the holding is separately and absolutely banned (see hedging).
rules.evidence: financial products (e.g. derivatives) that are issued or created by third parties over L1G shares or over any other securities issued by the Company

rules.detail: Absolute ban on derivative instruments or other products that operate to limit the economic risk of a Covered Person's holding in L1G Securities. Not limited to unvested or performance-conditioned securities, and not listed among the matters for which the Company Secretary may grant an exemption.
rules.evidence: Covered Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions: in derivative instruments or other products associated with L1G Securities which operate to limit the economic risk of their holding in L1G Securities

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a forward sale or similar structure that caps downside and/or upside operates to limit the economic risk of the holding, so it falls within the hedging ban.
rules.evidence: in derivative instruments or other products associated with L1G Securities which operate to limit the economic risk of their holding in L1G Securities

rules.detail: Ban extends beyond technical short selling to any arrangement that lets a Covered Person profit from a price decrease.
rules.evidence: which amount to 'short selling' of L1G Securities or otherwise enable a Covered Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of L1G Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not listed within the 'Trade' definition.

CFDs are not named, but as a financial product created by a third party over L1G shares they are L1G Securities, so a non-hedging, non-short CFD requires pre-authorisation; a CFD used to hedge or to profit from a price fall is caught by the hedging or short-selling bans instead.
rules.evidence: financial products (e.g. derivatives) that are issued or created by third parties over L1G shares or over any other securities issued by the Company

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over L1G Securities is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
No provision anywhere addresses secured financing arrangements in respect of L1G Securities.
Buying and selling, or selling and buying, within a six-month period is prohibited as short-term Trading, subject to the Company Secretary's discretionary exemption for special circumstances.
rules.evidence: Covered Persons must not engage in short-term Trading of any L1G Securities. Buying and selling (or selling and buying) within a six (6) month period is considered short-term.

external_documents: Platinum Investment Management Limited's Business Rules of Conduct (personal trading rules)
exemption_authority: Company Secretary may approve or deny, in their sole discretion, a written application for an exemption from the Closed Trading Period ban or the short-term trading ban where special circumstances exist (e.g. financial hardship or a court order). No exemption authority is stated for the hedging or short-selling prohibitions in section C(d).

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no provision addressing margin lending, other secured financing arrangements, or encumbrance of L1G Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The absence of any margin lending, secured financing or encumbrance restriction means a loan secured on the collared shares is not itself restricted by this policy, though the hedging ban still blocks the option overlay.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban not limited to unvested securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: in derivative instruments or other products associated with L1G Securities which operate to limit the economic risk of their holding in L1G Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban applies to a Covered Person's holding generally, not just unvested or performance-conditioned securities, so a collar over fully vested, unrestricted shares is caught just as much as one over unvested rights.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no closed-period relief for hedging or short selling
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Covered Person wishing to: Trade in L1G Securities ... during a Closed Trading Period; or engage in short-term Trading in L1G Securities, may apply in writing to the Company Secretary for an exemption if special circumstances exist
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company Secretary's exemption mechanism is limited to Closed Trading Period and short-term trading breaches; it does not extend to the section C(d) hedging or short-selling prohibitions, so there is no route to clear a collar even in special circumstances.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Platinum Covered Persons must obtain pre-authorisation ... Directors ... must obtain pre-authorisation ... by submitting a request to c&l@platinum.com.au ... All other Covered Persons ... must obtain pre-authorisation ... from the L1 Capital Head of Legal and Compliance
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Execution timing for any cleared dealing depends on which L1 Group entity a director or executive is affiliated with, and approvals are valid for only one Business Day regardless of route.

bespoke_clauses.topic: broad reach to controlled and beneficial interests
bespoke_clauses.clause: any account over which a Covered Person has an economic interest
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan written through a family trust, SMSF or other controlled vehicle is still caught, because the policy reaches any account in which a Covered Person or immediate family member has an economic or beneficial interest, or direct or indirect control.

summary: A funded collar's option legs are prohibited under this policy: section C(d) bars Covered Persons from entering into transactions in derivative instruments or other products associated with L1G Securities that operate to limit the economic risk of their holding, which squarely catches a purchased put and written call regardless of vesting state, and there is no clearance or exemption route for this prohibition (the Company Secretary's discretionary exemption applies only to breaches of the Closed Trading Period and short-term trading rules). By contrast, the policy is entirely silent on margin lending, secured financing and encumbrance of L1G Securities, so a loan secured on the collared shares is not itself restricted. Ordinary, non-hedging dealing in L1G Securities (including derivatives) by Covered Persons is permitted with one-Business-Day pre-clearance (route depending on the L1 Group entity involved), outside Closed Trading Periods and the six-month short-term trading window, and only while not aware of inside information. Because the hedging prohibition has no carve-out anywhere in the policy, a bank-funded collar cannot be implemented notwithstanding the complete absence of any restriction on the loan leg.
